name: ansible-lsp-client
description: Go-to-definition for Ansible file references, backed by a Rust language server.

ansibleLsp.inlayHints.enabled.description: Show the grey inline hints describing what a `when:` does on a run with no extra vars. Turn this off to remove the hints entirely. Diagnostics are unaffected.

ansibleLsp.hover.candidatesOnResolved.description: On hover over a reference that DID resolve, show the paths tried and mark the winner. Off by default the target is already a Cmd+click away. Turn on to see the full search order and which candidate won (useful for ambiguous roles and modules).

ansibleLsp.scan.concurrency.description: How many files the workspace scan analyses at once. 0 picks one per CPU core, which is best on a local disk. Raise it if your workspace is on a network share, a VM mount or WSL's /mnt/c, where files wait on the filesystem instead of working. Affects speed only, never what the scan reports. Applies to the next scan.

ansibleLsp.inventory.description: The inventory you run with, standing in for `-i` — which the editor cannot see. Paths are relative to the workspace folder; a directory reads every file in it, as ansible does. Leave empty to follow ANSIBLE_INVENTORY, then ansible.cfg's `inventory =`, then /etc/ansible/hosts, exactly as a plain `ansible-playbook` would. Set it when you habitually pass -i, since a different inventory can give the same variable a different value.

ansibleLsp.serverPath.description: Absolute path to the ansible-lsp binary. Defaults to ../target/release/ansible-lsp relative to this extension.

ansibleLsp.ansiblePath.description: Absolute path to the `ansible` package directory (the folder containing `modules/`), e.g. .../site-packages/ansible. Set this to pick which install to index when several exist, or when none is on PATH. Takes effect on reload. Leave empty to auto-detect (PATH, then uv/pipx tool dirs).

ansibleLsp.trace.server.description: Log LSP traffic to the 'Ansible LSP' output channel.
